# Week 7: EDA, Table 1 & AI Auditing {.unnumbered}

## Overview

This week builds the audit trail behind a descriptive analysis. You will define an analysis cohort, check missingness, create a Table 1-style summary, and audit a planted-error starter that mimics common AI-assisted mistakes.

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): WI-037, MIT-070, TF-020 — needs review -->
A Table 1 is a descriptive summary of the cohort before the main analysis. It usually shows who is included, key variables, missingness, and basic group summaries. It is not a causal result. Worked examples of every piece — cohort definition, exclusions, the missingness table, complete-case analysis, and a sample Table 1 — are in [eda02](eda02-cohort-and-missingness.qmd) and [eda03](eda03-worked-example.qmd).

EDA is treated as **evidence stewardship**: every exclusion, statistic, and interpretation should be visible enough for another person to rerun and challenge.

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): TF-020, MIT-075 — needs review -->
This week also revisits data provenance and Indigenous Data Sovereignty. The stewardship audit category ([eda05](eda05-ai-audit-categories.qmd)) asks the same questions you met with OCAP and CARE in [Week 1](../week01-health-data-ethics/index.qmd#indigenous-data-sovereignty): who has rights over this data, and does our use respect them?

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): MIT-086, TF-001 — needs review -->

- **Required (graded):** the six [Assignment 6](../../assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/README.md) files, explained one by one in [eda07](eda07-assignment-a6-and-reference.qmd), and the group [M2 preliminary analysis](../../milestones/m2-preliminary-analysis/README.md) due the same Monday.
- **Draft (studio work that feeds A6, not graded on its own):** the EDA note, missingness table, Table 1, and planted-error audit from [eda06](eda06-studio-planted-errors.qmd).

Tags like `[required]` and `[optional]` are defined in [How To Read Submission Lists](../../assignments/index.qmd#how-to-read-submission-lists).
:::

## Objectives

By the end of the week you can:

- define and document an analysis cohort before summarizing;
- report missingness for key variables rather than dropping rows silently;
- create a Table 1-style descriptive summary with N, mean, and SD;
- distinguish what descriptive statistics claim from what they cannot claim;
- audit code and prose for correctness, reproducibility, interpretation, and stewardship errors.

## Connection

Week 6 focused on whether visual design makes a descriptive claim honest and clear. Week 7 documents the cohort, missingness, and summary statistics behind those claims. Week 8 then turns one audited descriptive finding into a dashboard-style KT prototype.

## Case Study Data Analysis

The **NHANES Health Equity data spine** now supports code-reading, EDA, visualization, and reproducibility checks. Use the cached CSV/RDS for routine class work; a CDC retrieval script exists for advanced users.

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): MIT-036 — direct GitHub links so students can open the files without hunting through folders — needs review -->
- Cached RDS: [`examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.rds`](https://github.com/ehsanx/HDSx/blob/main/examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.rds)
- CSV snapshot: [`examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv`](https://github.com/ehsanx/HDSx/blob/main/examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv)
- Case-study README: [`examples/nhanes-equity/README.md`](https://github.com/ehsanx/HDSx/blob/main/examples/nhanes-equity/README.md)

The default classroom path is to use the cached data so the analysis work is reproducible without internet access.

**What to do here:** you may run the code below — it loads the cached CSV and prints two small summaries; reading it carefully is enough unless your week's page asks for more. <!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): MIT-025, MIT-050, MIT-061 — needs review -->


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse) # AI-EDIT(2026-06-23): tidyverse-default — consolidated core library() calls into library(tidyverse)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

nhanes_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(nhanes_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes_analysis <- read_csv(nhanes_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

nhanes_analysis |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    missing_bmi = sum(is.na(BMI)),
    missing_income = sum(is.na(IncomeGroup))
  )
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>     rows missing_bmi missing_income
#>    <int>       <int>          <int>
#> 1 105626        9356           9415

nhanes_analysis |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), Age >= 20, Age <= 80) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
#> # A tibble: 3 x 3
#>   IncomeGroup            n mean_bmi
#>   <chr>              <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 High Income (>3.5) 16330     28.6
#> 2 Low Income (<1.3)  15293     29.4
#> 3 Middle Income      19228     29.3
```
:::

## Class plan

1. Work through the [worked example](eda03-worked-example.qmd) using the CSV snapshot.
2. Name the cohort definition before inspecting any group summaries.
3. Build a missingness table for the variables used in the summary.
4. Produce a Table 1-style summary with N, BMI mean (SD), and age mean (SD).
5. Audit the planted-error starter in the [studio](eda06-studio-planted-errors.qmd) and categorize at least five issues.
6. Revise the methods note so provenance, missingness, and non-causal framing are explicit.

## Student output

By the end of class each student has a rerunnable EDA note, a Table 1-style summary, a planted-error audit, a provenance/stewardship note, and an AI-use note if AI helped draft code or prose.

## Links

- Assignment: [Assignment 6 — EDA and AI Audit](../../assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/README.md)

## Definition of done

- Cohort restrictions are stated before results are interpreted.
- Missingness is checked and reported before complete-case summaries are used.
- Table labels match the statistic actually computed.
- The audit identifies at least five planted issues across correctness, reproducibility, interpretation, and stewardship.
- M2 preliminary analysis renders from source and explains what the descriptive results do not prove.

## What students leave with

A reproducible EDA note and a habit of treating AI-generated summaries as drafts that must be checked against the data, code, and stewardship context.
